Let  
\[
\Omega=\{u\in\mathbb C:|u-c|<1\}.
\]

For distinct \(z,w\in\mathbb D\),
\[
F_\lambda(z)=F_\lambda(w)
\]
is equivalent to
\[
(z-w)\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{(z-c)(w-c)}\right)=0.
\]
Thus
\[
\lambda=(z-c)(w-c).
\]
Since \(u=c-z\) and \(v=c-w\) both lie in \(\Omega\), we have
\[
S_c=\{uv:u,v\in\Omega,\ u\ne v\}.
\]

The restriction \(u\ne v\) does not change the image: if \(u=v\in\Omega\), then for sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\),
\[
u+\varepsilon,\qquad \frac{u^2}{u+\varepsilon}
\]
are distinct points of \(\Omega\) whose product is \(u^2\). Hence
\[
S_c=\{uv:u,v\in\Omega\}.
\]

Set
\[
\alpha=\arcsin\frac1c.
\]
For \(-\alpha<\theta<\alpha\), the points of \(\Omega\) having argument \(\theta\) have moduli between
\[
q_-(\theta)=c\cos\theta-\sqrt{1-c^2\sin^2\theta}
\]
and
\[
q_+(\theta)=c\cos\theta+\sqrt{1-c^2\sin^2\theta}.
\]
Also,
\[
q_+(\theta)q_-(\theta)=c^2-1.
\]

If \(\lambda=uv\) has argument \(\phi\), write
\[
\arg u=\theta,\qquad \arg v=\phi-\theta.
\]
The maximal and minimal possible moduli of \(\lambda\) occur when
\[
\theta=\frac{\phi}{2}.
\]
Indeed, \(\log q_+(\theta)\) is strictly concave, since
\[
\frac{d^2}{d\theta^2}\log q_+(\theta)
=
-\frac{c\cos\theta}{(1-c^2\sin^2\theta)^{3/2}}<0.
\]
Therefore the radial bounds of \(S_c\) at angle \(\phi\), with \(|\phi|<2\alpha\), are
\[
R_{\rm out}(\phi)=q_+(\phi/2)^2,
\qquad
R_{\rm in}(\phi)=q_-(\phi/2)^2.
\]

Hence
\[
\operatorname{Area}(S_c)
=
\frac12\int_{-2\alpha}^{2\alpha}
\left(q_+(\phi/2)^4-q_-(\phi/2)^4\right)\,d\phi.
\]
Using symmetry and setting \(\theta=\phi/2\),
\[
\operatorname{Area}(S_c)
=
2\int_0^\alpha
\left(q_+(\theta)^4-q_-(\theta)^4\right)\,d\theta.
\]
Now
\[
q_+^4-q_-^4
=
8c\cos\theta\sqrt{1-c^2\sin^2\theta}
\left(2c^2\cos^2\theta-(c^2-1)\right).
\]
Let \(x=c\sin\theta\). Then
\[
\operatorname{Area}(S_c)
=
16\int_0^1
\sqrt{1-x^2}\,(c^2+1-2x^2)\,dx.
\]
Finally,
\[
\int_0^1\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx=\frac{\pi}{4},
\qquad
\int_0^1x^2\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx=\frac{\pi}{16},
\]
so
\[
\operatorname{Area}(S_c)
=
16\left((c^2+1)\frac{\pi}{4}-2\frac{\pi}{16}\right)
=
\boxed{2\pi(2c^2+1)}.
\]
